questions.question_text:
An aged-care support worker has a taxable income of $\$47\,850$.
What is her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Used $0.2$ instead of $0.02$ when converting $2\%$ to a decimal.
Used $0.002$, moving the decimal point one place too far when converting $2\%$.
Subtracted the levy from the taxable income instead of giving the levy itself.

questions.question_text:
A senior clinical psychologist has a taxable income of $\$163\,400$.
What is her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Halved the rate, charging $1\%$ of taxable income instead of $2\%$.
Charged $20$ cents in the dollar rather than $2$ cents in the dollar.
Applied the levy to the $\$180\,000$ tax-bracket boundary instead of to the taxable income.

questions.question_text:
A sports physiotherapist has a gross income of $\$92\,600$ and allowable tax deductions of $\$1850$.
What is his Medicare levy, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Charged the levy on gross income without subtracting the allowable deductions.
Added the deductions to the gross income instead of subtracting them.
Charged the levy on the deductions rather than on the taxable income.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Taxable income}=92\,600-1850$
$=\$90\,750$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times90\,750$
$=\$1815.00$

questions.question_text:
A pharmacist paid a Medicare levy of $\$1893.60$.
What was her taxable income, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Divided by $0.2$ instead of by $0.02$.
Divided by $0.002$, moving the decimal point one place too far.
Multiplied the levy by $20$ instead of dividing it by $0.02$.

questions.question_text:
A community aged-care worker has a taxable income of $\$58\,750$ and her income tax payable is $\$9338$.
What is her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the Medicare levy alone instead of adding it to the income tax payable.
Subtracted the levy from the income tax payable instead of adding it.
Added the levy to the taxable income rather than to the income tax payable.

questions.question_text:
A social worker's taxable income rises from $\$56\,400$ to $\$67\,900$.
How much more Medicare levy does she now pay, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the rise in taxable income rather than the extra levy charged on it.
Gave the levy on the new taxable income instead of the increase in the levy.
Charged $1\%$ of the rise instead of $2\%$.

questions.solution_text:
The levy rate is the same at both incomes, so only the increase is levied.
$\text{Extra levy}=0.02\times(67\,900-56\,400)$
$=0.02\times11\,500$
$=\$230.00$

questions.question_text:
An audiologist's income tax payable is $\$23\,415$ and her Medicare levy is $\$1860$.
What percentage of her total tax payable is the Medicare levy, to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Divided the levy by the income tax payable alone instead of by the total tax payable.
Gave the income tax’s share of the total tax rather than the levy’s share.
Quoted the levy rate of $2\%$ of taxable income instead of the levy’s share of the tax bill.

questions.question_text:
A hospital pharmacist has a taxable income of $\$84\,900$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Using the tax table, what is her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Gave the income tax payable only and left the Medicare levy out of the total.
Subtracted the Medicare levy from the income tax instead of adding it.
Taxed the whole income at $32.5$c instead of only the excess over $\$45\,000$ before adding the levy.
